items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline says what to do (keep September) and why: both candidates cost 27–28% more and neither stays in character more often. The first claim is now c1, the cost finding that decides the call. Recommendation gives September's price ($1.89 per 1,000 replies). Why_not separates the two candidates correctly. Watch carries the main risks: September holds character in only 65.8% of off-lane replies, the earlier qwen3.8-flash cost finding fails here, and 1017's reasoning share is 55% against September's 76%. The flag puts the late criteria on the first screen.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 (cost decides, corrected) leads to c2 (pass rate inside the 15-point margin), c3 (corrected character drops), c4 (off-lane carries 48% and 53% of the in-character loss, per measure_breakdown) and c5 (how off-lane fails). The explore row agrees with decision_sensitivity: the call holds at every margin, with flips at 10.8 and 5.8. options_dominance names September as dominant. One small seam remains. The headline's 27–28% reads the per-arm means: $2.427 and $2.406 against $1.892, a $0.535 gap for qwen3.8-flash. c1's own forest shows a paired +$0.616 (about 33%), and no line reconciles the two (see findings).

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: September's weak axis is on the first screen: 65.8% in character off-lane, failing the same way as the candidates. 1017's character gap is now stated at its true size: one of four judged figures is separated (in-character -4.7, -8.2 to -1.3); pass rate (-3.0, -7.4 to +1.3), outcome and transcript are not. c4 labels its unpaired, uncorrected strata as leads. A few phrasings still run a little ahead of the evidence, none on a deciding interval. The lede's 'more cases would not move it' means 'would not reverse it'. 'Only a candidate priced below September would reopen the call', repeated in decision.next and next[0], ignores a future candidate that is better on character. c5's 'rather than in a new one' generalises from the first three kept failures per arm.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Every omission checks out against the snapshot. Booth-offstage, delivery and failed-reply notices are unseparated for both arms in contrasts_list. Outcome and transcript are separated for qwen3.8-flash only, and the entry now says so. Both floors hold (readings_list: worst drops 10.8 and 7.1 against 15). The other 22 strata are 17 cases or fewer, and 19 of them hold 10 or fewer (measure_breakdown). There is no price trade, because options_dominance has September dominating both candidates. Nothing omitted changes the call.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The reasoning-ratio confound (scoped to 1017) appears in confidence, in watch and in next[5]. That step says it would not change the call, which cost decides. confound:model is shown not to matter: levers_effects reports model as the only setting the arms vary, and it is isolated. The simulator settings caveat goes to next[4]. The uncalibrated judge goes to next[3]. The short runs (two trials lost) are bounded against a separated drop. The unequal cost trial sets, flagged in round 1, are now bounded in Method/Cost and paired in the c1 forest.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each of the six steps names an action and what it settles: reconcile the earlier cost finding's control and prices; pre-declare the aspect, control, margin and floor; rewrite the off-lane directive and re-run on September; calibrate the judge on human ratings; record the simulator settings; run 1017 with its reasoning share matched to September's.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c2's readings forest with the margin line, c3's corrected forest and c4's labelled unpaired strata bars each fit their claim, and the counterfactual holds for them. Two fits are weaker. First, c1 pairs bars with a $0.535 gap for qwen3.8-flash ($2.427 vs $1.892) with a forest showing +$0.616 for the same comparison. Neither caption says why they differ (paired on shared conversations vs unpaired means over 864, 828 and 879 trials), and the forest's interval prints at uneven precision (+$0.3791, +$0.1743, +$0.8105). Second, c5's block is the snapshot's first three kept failures per arm, out of 39, 64 and 62 (examples_list keeps the first per slice, not a sample). It shows that the kept failures look alike. It cannot show that the candidates fail 'in the same way rather than in a new one': if the other 156 failures differed, this block would read the same.

findings.finding: The headline and c1 put the uplift at 27–28%, read from per-arm means over unequal trial sets ($2.427 and $2.406 vs $1.892). c1's paired, corrected forest shows +$0.616 per 1,000 for qwen3.8-flash (about 33%) and +$0.492 for 1017 (about 26%). A reader comparing the two blocks sees a $0.535 gap in the bars and $0.616 in the forest with no explanation. Either quote the paired range (about 26–33%), or add a caption line saying the forest pairs conversations where both arms reported a cost, so its gap differs from the difference of the bars. Also round the forest's interval ends to the precision of its point estimates.

'So the candidates fail more often in the same way rather than in a new one' generalises from the snapshot's first three kept failures per arm (3 of 39, 3 of 64, 3 of 62). The pool takes each slice's first failure, so it is not a sample. Scope it: the kept failures look alike, a lead. Or drop the 'rather than a new one' clause. next[2]'s directive rewrite stands either way, since September's own off-lane rate is 65.8%.

The lede says more cases 'would not move' the extra cost. It means they would not reverse it, since the corrected intervals clear zero (+$0.379 and +$0.174 per 1,000 at their low ends). The lede, decision.next and next[0] also say only a candidate priced below September would reopen the call. For the candidates tested that is true. A future candidate that is better on character could reopen it too, as the judge_uncalibrated caveat's own wording concedes. Say 'of these candidates' or 'a candidate no worse on character and cheaper'.

invariant_concerns: All 38 figure keys the report cites read through figure_keys_check, with no refusals. Every report-reach caveat (late:aspect, late:control, late:margin, late:floor, judge_uncalibrated) appears in confidence, either with a material_if clause or as checked immaterial, and the scoped caveats appear too. The form is high_if_immaterial while caveats are open, which satisfies invariant 4.

Invariant 5 (unchanged from round 1): the two short_run caveat ids carry run UUIDs (short_run:01a170ab-..., short_run:01a17121-...), and the late:floor id carries a measure-style key ('character adherence (v2)/rate_drop/*'). If the page renders caveat ids above the appendix, invariant 5 fails. The caveat text itself names no id.
